title: heap-buffer-overflow in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint
live_proof: backport filter: upstream fix adfb203a7d ("Fix a buffer overread in fts5 ... ORDER BY rowid DESC ... corrupt database records") removes code still present in 3.22.0, and its own regression database (decoded from the fix's hex dump) reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as heap-buffer-overflow in sqlite3Fts5GetVarint (results/2026-10-11-host-asan). Recorded as heap-use-after-free until 2026-10-15: the over-read lands in a freed neighbour of the page, and an earlier heap layout put it inside that block, which ASan names a use-after-free (PROVENANCE.md)
arena_bytes_why: 1 MiB on every arm. Five of the eight spatial cases are forced here by reachability -- at 262144 cases 21, 22 and 23 exhaust memsys5 before the defect (pcache1AllocPage dereferences the NULL that 3.22.0 does not check), 29 returns SQLITE_NOMEM, and 00 takes a different path -- so the same value is declared for all eight to keep the arms comparable. Measured 2026-10-17; this is also the value every recorded virtual reading was taken at, while CheriBSD had been running 262144.
object: the fts5 leaf-page buffer fts5SegIterReverse keeps as pLast, live at the access
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt leaf's header carries a first-rowid offset past the end of the page (iOff=148 on a 24-byte page), and fts5SegIterReverse hands it to the varint decoder unchecked
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: upstream's own regression image, run statement by statement through stock 3.22.0. Served from repro322_memfs.c rather than a real file -- ext/misc/memvfs.c cannot be used, it serves only the main database so the pager cannot create a rollback journal, and it takes its buffer as an integer in the URI, which on a capability machine is an untagged forged pointer

sublet.oracle: VM HALTED on a capability fault, cause 24 untagged dereference (temporal: revoked, or never a capability) pc=0x800239e4 -- taken outside the domain, so cooperative recovery has no frame to return through; all 28 halts in this arm are at the same kernel pc 0x800239e4
